title: Probabilistic admission controller and token-density KV compaction for mixed-turn continuous batching
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts followed by long generated responses, or vice versa) cause inefficient slot utilization in the continuous batcher and lead to KV cache pressure and GPU memory fragmentation. This ticket experiments with a probabilistic admission controller that accepts or delays incoming requests based on a lightweight token-density estimate and a length-population model, combined with a token-density-driven KV compaction policy that aggressively compacts low-utility KV entries to reclaim GPU slab space without hurting hit-rate for hot prefixes. Goal: reduce tail latency for short critical requests, improve overall throughput for long responses, and decrease out-of-memory incidents on medium-sized V100/A100 nodes.
success_criteria: 10-20% reduction in 99th percentile latency for short-turn requests under mixed traffic
5-10% improvement in average token throughput on 8xA100 workers during long-response steady-state
reduction in KV-induced OOM events to zero in canary cluster
approach: Admission controller: probabilistic admission with tunable base delay. For each incoming request we compute a token-density score = expected_output_tokens / (expected_context_tokens + 1). Use a short moving window of observed paired request-response lengths to estimate distribution per route.

If token-density > high_threshold, admit immediately to favor high-throughput long responses. If token-density < low_threshold and current slot occupancy > soft_target, probabilistically delay admission by sampling from an exponential backoff distribution scaled to slot pressure.
Soft quotas: assign soft KV reservation budgets per slot cohort (short, medium, long) rather than hard static reservations to prevent long requests starving short-turn throughput.

KV compaction: maintain per-key utility score (recency * response-length-weighted-hit-rate). Periodically compact keys below a dynamic utility percentile. Compaction is token-density-aware: more aggressive compaction during high token-density phases.

GPU memory management: perform defragmentation during low-util windows via coordinated slab repacking triggered when free contiguous memory falls below watermark. Ensure repacking is interruptible and has an abort path if latency SLOs tighten.
Simulation: run discrete-event simulation using recorded traffic traces from 'multi-turn-mix-2026-q1' to validate tuning knobs before canary.
Gradual rollout: feature flag behind rollout with canary on 5% of traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> full, with automated rollback if tail latency regresses >5% or OOMs occur.
experiments_and_results: 2026-02-25: Microbench on 4xA100 emulated mixed traffic (40% short prompts producing short responses, 60% short prompts with long responses). Baseline: 99p short latency=210ms. After admission controller: 99p short latency=175ms (-17%). Throughput unchanged within noise.

2026-03-01: KV compaction stress test on 8xV100 nodes with synthetic churn. Baseline kv-residency=78% of slab. After compaction policy: kv-residency=61%, observed small drop in cache-hit for very long prefixes (2.3% absolute), but end-to-end token cost decreased 8%.

2026-03-05: Combined canary on prod-west-canary (5%). Observed 12% reduction in short-request tail latency, 6% throughput increase for long-response flows, zero OOMs during 72h test. One regression: route /agent-stream-verbose saw 3% increase in median latency due to compaction causing KV-prefetch misses; mitigated by raising utility floor for that route.
Notes: simulation correlated with prod canary on short-tail improvements but underestimated compaction impact on low-frequency long prefixes.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Probabilistic delays can increase perceived latency for some short requests if thresholds mis-calibrated — mitigate with strict SLO guardrails for high-priority routes.

Aggressive KV compaction reduces memory pressure but risks increased recomputation when rare prefixes are requested; mitigated via per-route utility floors and detection of low-frequency heavy hitters.
GPU repacking is intrusive and may transiently increase latency; schedule during low-load windows and ensure abort semantics.
Feature complexity increases operational surface; require additional observability (per-cohort admission rates, compaction churn, slab fragmentation metrics).
implementation_notes: Admission controller implemented as lightweight pre-batcher hook; target CPU overhead < 0.5% of request path.
Token-density estimation uses exponential moving average with 30s half-life per route to adapt quickly to diurnal shifts.
Utility scoring stored as compact 32-bit floats in host-side metadata to avoid additional GPU allocations.
Compaction runs as background bounded tasks with backpressure to avoid saturating PCIe during repack.
Added metric labels: batcher_cohort, admission_action {admit, delay, reject}, kv_compaction_pass_id, slab_fragmentation_pct.
open_tasks: Tune low/high thresholds per-route and expose knobs in console UI (PM/Console work required)
Add automated detection of per-route regressions and rollback trigger (SRE)
Implement metrics dashboard and alerts: 99p by cohort, compaction churn, slab fragmentation, reservation utilization
Extend simulation harness to include weighted user cohorts and longer tail distributions
Write canary runbook and post-mortem checklist for repacking failures
